name: step1b-feature-engineering
notes: STEP 1b of the data selection, between step 1 (tradable dates) and step 2 (feature availability): the engineered per-date feature panel. Inputs are the prepared panel step 1 read (pipeline.source), step 1's selected.jsonl (step1_selection, onboarded as for step 2) and the reader's own sources (pipeline.panel, the ADR-0203 tail-data block). Per ticker in foreach.keys it keeps step 1's cohort rows at step 1's selected DTE (read from selected.jsonl, never typed; row count pinned to step 1's listed_forecasts) and attaches four families: variance_gap, ohlc_shape, positioning_changes, expanded_volatility_context, plus the expiry-density count. Output: input_panel.jsonl, one row per ticker/quote_date/expiry of that cohort, every prepared-panel field unchanged plus the engineered ones. A field that cannot be computed or whose entry-time availability cannot be established is an explicit null with its reason in fe_<entry>_reasons; fe_<family>_status says whether the row's identity was found. Per-family summaries and clock notes land in carry.json (features__<t>.summary and .provenance, panel.provenance). All open-interest-derived fields are withheld until the OI publication clock is audited. Weekday one-hot waits for ADR-0214 (pending_inputs). AMZN is out of scope until its close-source ADR lands. Step 2 consumes this panel by changing only its source root (see the plan runbook).

source.notes: The prepared option panel step 1 read, same root/source/stream. There is deliberately no ts_field: ObservationRows would stamp quote_date_ms into every row and refuse a row that already carries it, and step 2 stamps its own when it reads this step's output.

step1_selection.notes: The onboarded selected.jsonl, exactly as step 2 reads it: the selected DTE and its row count come from here.

panel.notes: The tail-data panel read (ADR-0203's data block, values unchanged), once for every ticker, narrowed to the identity, agreed and engineered columns; it calls the existing ExactExpiryCDFPanel.read() and restates no formula. archive_root (the raw-chain prepare stage), fred_market_symbols (macro is not an engineered family) and the market series no family uses are left out. Its columns must equal what the attach node expects, or the attach refuses. surface, lifecycle and chain_features are store references (source, stream, relpath) resolved against root, the onboarding store.

params.provenance_waiver: each row carries its own symbol; the key check proves no ticker appears twice

panel_rows.notes: The tickers' engineered rows as one stream for the writer.

params.provenance_waiver: each selection row carries its own symbol

expected_rows.notes: One step-1 winner row per ticker, to total their listed_forecasts.

expected_sum.notes: Step 1's settled-row count at the winning DTE, summed over the tickers run: the number of rows this step must write.

params.source: Step-1 cohort rows at the selected exact DTE with engineered features; onboarded through source-feature-panel.json as step 2's data source

panel_evidence.notes: The step 1b output. expect pins the row count to step 1's listed_forecasts, so a source or ticker that changed between the steps refuses. The parent directory must exist (mkdir -p) and the writer refuses to overwrite; to repeat, move pipeline_runs/feature-engineering and feature-panel-source aside.

weekday_onehot.reason: ADR-0214's weekday-onehot kind is not merged; after it merges add one template node using it on $features.records (date_field quote_date) and feed panel_rows from it. Its code is never copied here.

pending_inputs.notes: Declared, not computed: an input this step is waiting for.

foreach.notes: The only ticker setting: symbols present in the prepared panel and in step 1's selected.jsonl (each must have a winner row or the run refuses); keep it equal to step 1's keys. AMZN is out of scope until its close-source ADR lands.

selection.notes: This ticker's winner row from step 1.

selected_dte.notes: The DTE this step runs at, read from step 1. A ticker absent from step 1 leaves a dangling reference below and the run refuses.

cohort.notes: Step 1's settled-row predicate at step 1's DTE. No feature clause may be added here: features are attached to the cohort, never used to choose it.

horizon_rows.notes: Every settled expiry of this ticker listed within the selected horizon, BEFORE the cohort filter (a cohort-first count would be 1 on every row). The bound is the planned calendar_dte: it is known at entry from regular holidays, where the actual settlement date is label information.

dense.notes: A date whose only cohort expiry has a planned DTE above the selected one (an unscheduled closure moved its settlement earlier) gets a declared null, counted in the summary.

variance_gap.clock_note: same-date entry-chain ATM IV against backward 22-session realized volatility over the planned sessions to expiry (regular holidays, never ad hoc closures); after-close estimand

ohlc_shape.clock_note: entry bar plus backward 5- and 22-session windows from the local OHLC source; the entry bar is known only after that close (after-close estimand, not intraday); raw prices, so an ex-dividend gap shows in overnight_return

positioning_changes.clock_note: entry-snapshot volume and spread plus the prior observation's open interest of the same expiry series (known at entry under either OI convention; built per calendar year, so a series' first observation in a year has no lag); the three OI x greek fields are withheld: entry-snapshot open interest; its publication clock is unverified, so the field is withheld until one audit shows archive open_interest excludes the entry day's trades (one audit for positioning, liquidity and chain nodes)

expanded_volatility_context.clock_note: last Cboe index close strictly before the entry date, at most 7 calendar days old, else null; a prior-date close is published before the entry close; the retrospective download vintage is not certified; VXN is omitted as QQQ's own_iv; IWM's market_rvx is its own RVX from the prior date

expiry_density.clock_note: listed expiries with planned settlement 1 to the selected DTE calendar days after entry; the panel keeps only expiries with an observed settlement path and a defined rv_22, so an expiry dropped for a missing close is uncounted (incomplete_path, missing_reference in the reader's refused size the loss)

liquidity_oi.clock_note: liquidity family OI columns on the prepared panel: entry-snapshot open interest; its publication clock is unverified, so the field is withheld until one audit shows archive open_interest excludes the entry day's trades (one audit for positioning, liquidity and chain nodes)

chain_nodes_oi.clock_note: chain-node OI columns on the prepared panel: entry-snapshot open interest; its publication clock is unverified, so the field is withheld until one audit shows archive open_interest excludes the entry day's trades (one audit for positioning, liquidity and chain nodes)

oi_panel_columns.clock_note: panel columns in no step-2 contract that still hold the same OI (chain_liquidity_asymmetry is the tanh of chain_log_put_call_oi): entry-snapshot open interest; its publication clock is unverified, so the field is withheld until one audit shows archive open_interest excludes the entry day's trades (one audit for positioning, liquidity and chain nodes)

features.notes: Attaches the reader's families to the cohort by ticker/date/expiry. agree_fields are fields both sources hold and must equal on a matched identity, so a prepared panel and a reader built from different sources refuse. max_absent_fraction 0 refuses any cohort row the reader lacks; raise it only to a fraction the refusal message reports and you have explained. A withheld field is null on every row with its reason in fe_<entry>_reasons; lifting a withhold is a JSON edit citing the audit. The prepared panel must carry every carried field (a null is allowed, a missing key is not).
